title: Privilege propagation and scope-mapping model for RBAC v2
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Purpose: Define a pragmatic, auditable RBAC v2 model that supports fine-grained resource hierarchies, explicit scope mappings, deterministic privilege propagation, and smooth migration from RBAC v1. Scope: role model, permission tuple shape, propagation semantics, evaluation order, audit annotations, SSO/SAML attribute mapping guidance, and admin guardrails. Non-goals: complete policy language (OPA-style) or a full ABAC engine — we will provide attribute hints and constraint expressions but keep evaluation primarily role-and-scope based.

Core concepts: 
- Resource lattice: every resource type (project, deployment, model, customer-tenant, route) exposes a typed path (e.g., /org/{org}/project/{proj}/model/{model}) and a set of anchor points that can be used for binding roles. The lattice supports non-tree relationships via alias links (e.g., dedicated-capacity -> pool) but evaluation prefers canonical paths.
- Scope anchor: a canonical binding point used by role bindings. Anchors are first-class and are what the permission matrix targets.
- Permission tuple: (action, resource-pattern, constraint-expression, effect). Example: ("write:invoke", "/org/*/project/*/model/*", "if request.origin == 'console'", "allow"). 
- Inheritance modes: strict (children inherit exactly), overlay (children combine parent grants but can add denies), delegated (explicit delegation tokens required). Each role binding specifies an inheritance mode.
- Propagation rules: privileges propagate down the lattice by default only for roles marked as "propagate: true". Deny entries are globally authoritative and follow deny-overrides semantics.

Decision summary: 
1) Deny-overrides: explicit deny wins. This reduces surprise for admin guardrails.
2) Evaluation order: find direct bindings on resource -> evaluate inherited bindings (respecting inheritance_mode) -> evaluate group and SAML mappings -> apply deny overrides -> resolve final allow/deny. This is stable and cache-friendly.
3) Role composition: roles are first-class sets of permission tuples; we allow role composition (role includes other roles) but composition must be acyclic.
4) Audit annotations: every evaluation emits a structured audit event with these fields: evaluator_version, principal_id, principal_origin (SSO/ServiceToken), resolved_roles(list), binding_ids(list), permission_tuple_matched, cache_hit (true/false), policy_revision, trace_id. These must be included in request logs and exported to audit pipeline.

Permission matrix (example excerpt):
- Admin: allow * on /org/* (propagate: true)
- Tenant-Owner: allow create/update/delete on /org/{o}/project/* (propagate: true)
- Model-Runner: allow invoke on /org/{o}/project/{p}/model/* (propagate: false)
- Billing-Reader: allow read on /org/{o}/billing (propagate: false)
- Audit-Observer: allow read on /org/*/audit-logs (propagate: false, effect: allow, constraints: "read-only")

SSO/SAML & provisioning guidance: 
- Attribute mapping: prefer group and role attributes in SAML assertions. Recommended assertion attributes: groups, role-ids, org-id, preferred_username, email_verified. 
- Group-to-role mapping: mapping rules live in the control plane (customer-managed). Mappings are versioned. For shadow rollout we will support a mapping sandbox for customers to preview mapped roles vs current v1. 
- SCIM/Provisioning: we support SCIM for long-lived group/role sync and recommend short-lived SAML assertions for session binding. 
- Security control: disallow remote role elevation based solely on email domain; require matching org-id for high-privilege grants.

Admin controls & guardrails: 
- Breakglass roles: emergency roles issued via an auditable one-time token flow requiring justification, expiration, and 2FA. All breakglass issuance emits a high-fidelity audit event flagged for compliance queues.
- Two-person approval: for any role grant that contains permissions marked as "sensitive" (e.g., export PII, change billing), enforce 2 approvers before activation. 
- Read-only auditor: a builtin role that can access policy, bindings, and full evaluation traces but cannot alter policies.

Migration plan from RBAC v1: 
- Phase 1: Canonicalization. Introduce anchors for v1 bindings and surface implicit resource paths. 
- Phase 2: Shadow evaluation. Run RBAC v2 evaluation in parallel with v1 for all requests and record divergences post-auth. Divergences get triaged into a migration backlog.
- Phase 3: Controlled switch with feature-flag per-org. Allow customers to opt into v2, with a telemetry dashboard showing divergence rate and blocked requests.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Functional: RBAC v2 evaluation returns identical decisions as v1 for 99.9% of requests for an org in the canonicalization phase (where intended). Divergences are logged and explainable. 
- Performance: median decision latency <= 1.2x v1 baseline at 95th percentile for orgs with up to 5k bindings. 
- Observability: all evaluations emit audit events with required fields and are queryable in the console. 
- Security: breakglass issuance requires 2FA and emits an immutable audit trail. 

Notes on trade-offs: 
- We chose deny-overrides to keep guardrails simple; this may require more explicit allows in complex overlays. 
- Allowing role composition reduces duplication but increases evaluation graph complexity; we mitigate via acyclic enforcement and caching. 
- Adding constraint-expressions increases expressivity but is limited to simple request-local checks to avoid embedding a full policy language.

Deliverables: design doc, canonicalizer library, evaluation engine changes, audit-event schema changes, SAML mapping UI, migration dashboard, E2E tests and perf benchmarks.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Design doc reviewed and approved by Security and Privacy. 2) Shadow-eval framework logs divergences and a dashboard surfaces top 50 divergence classes. 3) End-to-end perf tests demonstrate <=1.2x median decision latency vs v1 at 95th percentile. 4) Audit events emitted for 100% of evaluated requests with required fields. 5) Breakglass flow implemented with 2FA and telemetry flagging.
technical_decisions: Evaluation order: direct -> inherited -> mapped -> deny resolution
Role composition allowed with acyclic check
Scoped propagation controlled via propagate flag on role bindings
Audit event schema must include evaluator_version, resolved_roles, binding_ids, cache_hit, policy_revision
implementation_plan: Phase A: publish design doc and schema; security review
Phase B: implement canonicalizer and anchor model; add DB migration for anchors
Phase C: engine changes - inheritance modes and propagation flags; implement deny-overrides logic
Phase D: audit pipeline changes; add evaluation trace fields and exports
Phase E: SAML/SCIM mapping UI and sandbox; rollout dashboard and shadow-eval
Phase F: gradual org opt-in and full switch; deprecate v1 bindings after 3 months
risk_mitigation: Shadow evaluation with divergence triage to avoid regressions
Per-org feature flags to roll back quickly
Performance budgets and circuit-breakers to fall back to v1 evaluation if v2 path exceeds latency thresholds
Automated E2E tests against representative org datasets to catch edge cases
test_plan: Unit tests for propagation rules, inheritance modes, and deny behavior
Integration tests exercising SAML mappings + SCIM sync
Shadow-eval replay tests comparing v1 and v2 outputs across sampled production traces
Load tests for decision latency with synthetic orgs (1k, 5k, 25k bindings)
Audit-event integrity checks and backwards-compat export tests
rollout_plan: Internal dogfood in staging orgs for 2 weeks
Shadow-eval for 50 beta customers for 4 weeks with weekly divergence review
Opt-in for broader customers behind console toggle; communicate migration guide
Full default switch after 3 months if divergence < 0.1% for participating customers
